title: Quantify impact of rate-limit burst-smoothing on per-model usage heatmaps and correct attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After enabling the adaptive rate-limit burst-smoothing heuristic in the ingest path to reduce quota noise, we observed persistent troughs and misattributed per-model heatmap rows for a subset of tenants when the system performs partial backfills. This ticket quantifies the problem, identifies the root cause, and implements a remediation path that preserves smoothing for enforcement but stores raw tokens for analytics and backfill correction.
acceptance_criteria: Console per-model daily charts show <=0.5% divergence vs raw token counts for 99% of tenants over a 7-day window after migration
Backfilled windows that previously showed valley artifacts are reconstructed to within 1 token per 1000 tokens of original raw stream for sampled tenants
No increase in enforcement latency >50ms p50 after changes to ingestion path
Add a dashboard comparing raw vs smoothed counts and a flag column for 'smoothing_applied' visible to platform engineers
steps_taken: Reproduced issue against prod reconstructed dataset using synthetic tenant B (high short bursts) and compared console heatmaps to raw ledger exports
Added temporary debug tag 'smoothing_delta' to a small percentage of traffic to capture before/after counts (rolled for 48 hours)
Ran three ad-hoc SQL queries in BigQuery to compute per-model diffs and time-of-day alignment (queries linked in related_links)
Created a staging replay of a 2-hour burst window to test deterministic reconstruction logic
analysis_findings: Root cause: burst-smoothing algorithm applies a sliding normalization window that mutates ingestion events in-place for quota enforcement, but we were discarding the original raw_token_count field. Analytics previously read the normalized stream, so short high-burst tenants show permanent valleys until a full backfill reconstructs raw events.

Secondary cause: shard-coalescing in the ingestion layer can drop smoothing metadata when events cross shard boundaries during rollovers, causing under-attribution in per-model breakdowns for multi-shard bursts
Observed effect size: for synthetic tenant B, peak-hour aggregate undercount was 6.8% in per-model charts and produced visible troughs that lasted 2–8 hours depending on backfill cadence
Enforcement accuracy: smoothing prevented quota oscillation but mutation cost is high for analytics. Enforcement latency impact from additional metadata tagging is negligible in staging (+8ms p50).
proposed_solution: Short-term (hotfix): stop in-place destructive normalization. Persist a raw_token_count and smoothing_applied boolean on every ingest event. Recompute analytics to prefer raw_token_count if present. Ship within 1 sprint to reduce live divergence.

Medium-term: add a non-destructive smoothing layer that surfaces a derived 'smoothed_for_quota' stream for enforcement consumers while preserving a canonical raw event stream for downstream analytics and backfills.

Backfill migration: implement a one-shot reconstruction job that replays 72 hours of smoothed events and repopulates analytics tables with raw_token_count. Run in a throttled manner to avoid OOMs. Create a migration plan with monitoring and rollback.
Long-term: redesign shard-cutover handoff semantics so smoothing metadata is checkpointed and atomically transferred during shard rotations to eliminate boundary-loss cases
Instrumentation: add console charts that show smoothed vs raw counts, plus a per-tenant 'smoothing_ratio' metric and an alert if ratio deviates >2% for production tenants
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge PR with non-destructive event enrichment (adds raw_token_count, smoothing_applied) to staging. Test end-to-end with replay of synthetic bursts and run LUCI integration tests.

Week 1: Deploy to canary (5% of traffic) and launch a compare dashboard to validate that console per-model charts now read raw_token_count. Monitor enforcement latencies and quota behavior for regressions.
Week 2: If canary passes, expand to 50% and run the 72-hour reconstruction job for a representative shard subset. Validate reconciliations vs original ledger exports.

Week 3: Full rollout to prod ingestion and schedule the full 72-hour backfill migration in low-traffic window (UTC 02:00–06:00). Post-migration, turn on concerns dashboard and remove temporary debug tags after 7 days.
Rollback: if enforcement regressions or latency > 50ms p50 observed, revert enrichment and fall back to previous smoothing behavior while investigating shard handoff fixes
notes: This ticket intentionally separates enforcement-from-analytics to keep quota stability while restoring attribution accuracy
We must coordinate with SRE for the backfill migration (runbook, throttles, memory limits).
Notify customer success and engineering leads for tenants in the top-100 by usage so they expect short visibility changes in their charts during the migration window
